name: DocVQA
description: A dataset for Visual Question Answering on document images consisting of 50,000 questions defined on 12,767 document images of varied types and content.
creator: Minesh Mathew, Dimosthenis Karatzas, C.V. Jawahar
citeAs: Mathew, Minesh, Dimosthenis Karatzas, and C.V. Jawahar. "DocVQA: A Dataset for VQA on Document Images." arXiv:2007.00398v3, 2021.
rai:dataCollection: Document images were sourced from documents in the UCSF Industry Documents Library. The authors downloaded documents from different collections and hand picked pages for use in the dataset, prioritizing non-binarized pages and pages with tables, forms, lists and figures. Questions and answers were collected with the help of remote workers using a web-based annotation tool in three stages: stage 1 collected up to 10 question-answer pairs per image; stage 2 verified questions by collecting answers independently and assigning one or more question types; stage 3 reviewed cases where answers from stages 1 and 2 did not exactly match, and this review was done by the authors.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Document images are drawn from pages of 6,071 industry documents from the UCSF Industry Documents Library, spanning five industries: tobacco, food, drug, fossil fuel and chemical.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The authors hand picked pages from downloaded documents, tried to minimize binarized images because of poor image quality, and prioritized pages with tables, forms, lists and figures over pages containing only running text. The data was split randomly in an 80-10-10 ratio into train, validation and test splits.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For experiments, OCR tokens were extracted using a commercial OCR application. For BERT question answering, OCR tokens recognized on document images were serialized into a single string separated by spaces in top-left to bottom-right order, and answer spans were approximated by finding the first match of the answer string in the serialized OCR string.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Questions and answers were collected with remote workers using a web-based annotation tool. In stage 1, workers were shown a document image and asked to define at most 10 question-answer pairs, with instructions to ask questions answerable using text present in the image and to enter the answer verbatim from the document; they were encouraged to add more than one ground truth answer when warranted. In stage 2, another worker was shown the image and the questions from stage 1, but not the answers, and was required to enter answers and assign one or more question types to each question. Workers could flag inapt questions due to language issues or ambiguity, and such questions were excluded. In stage 3, if none of the answers from stage 1 exactly matched any answers from stage 2, the question was sent for review, where questions and answers were editable and the reviewer either accepted or ignored the item. The third-stage review was done by the authors.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The second stage independently verified answers from the first stage and assigned question types. If none of the answers entered in the first stage matched exactly with any of the answers from the second stage, the question was sent for third-stage review by the authors, who could edit questions and answers before accepting or ignoring them. Questions flagged in stage 2 for language issues or ambiguity were not included in the dataset.
rai:annotationsPerItem: Up to 10 question-answer pairs could be created per document image in stage 1; each question then received an independent answer in stage 2, and mismatched cases were reviewed in stage 3.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Remote workers; a few volunteers from the authors' institution were used for measuring human performance on the test split.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset, code and leaderboard are available at docvqa.org.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The documents originate from five industries and span many decades; examples and analysis indicate named entities such as names of people, institutions and places appear in answers.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is introduced to inspire a purpose-driven approach in document image analysis and recognition research, encouraging methods that use low-level cues and high-level goals to solve problems of practical importance.
rai:dataBiases: The authors tried to minimize binarized images and prioritized pages with tables, forms, lists and figures over pages with only running text. They also used many documents from food and nutrition related collections because they had a good number of non-binarized images. Most documents are from the 1960-2000 period.
rai:dataLimitations: Majority of documents in the source library are binarized and binarization has affected image quality. OCR errors impact answers, including over-segmentation and incorrect recognition. Existing models perform poorly on questions requiring understanding of document structure, figures, diagrams, photographs and handwriting. The paper notes that answers are not always exactly matched due to OCR imperfections, motivating use of ANLS instead of exact accuracy alone.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for Visual Question Answering on document images and for evaluating document understanding methods. It is split into train, validation and test sets in an 80-10-10 ratio: train has 39,463 questions and 10,194 images, validation has 5,349 questions and 1,286 images, and test has 5,188 questions and 1,287 images.
